rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most important uncertainty is the performance floor of each modality, which is needed before evaluating whether fusion or more complex encoders add value. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible RNA baseline: no aggregation, no fusion, a standard linear encoder. It establishes the RNA-only reference accuracy against which all subsequent RNA encoder choices (scvi, scgpt), profile settings (multiprofile), and multimodal fusion experiments can be compared. Starting with the simplest configuration avoids confounding multiple design changes and gives a clean anchor point for the 9 remaining experiments.

The only completed experiment (config_001, RNA-only/singleprofile/pca_n2000) yielded ~48.5% accuracy, giving a weak baseline with high uncertainty about which design axes matter most. The single most consequential question is whether the image modality carries any discriminative signal for this task. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image modality with a standard encoder and the same single-profile structure as config_001, making it a clean one-variable comparison. If image-only accuracy is substantially different from the RNA baseline, it tells me whether multimodal fusion is worth investing the remaining 8 experiments in, or whether I should focus on RNA encoder/profile improvements. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the tight budget.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieves 0.485 accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is very weak at 0.208, confirming RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether a learned RNA representation (scvi) can improve upon the linear PCA_n2000 baseline. This experiment (config_004: rna_only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) isolates the effect of the RNA encoder by changing only that one variable relative to config_001. If scvi_n200 substantially outperforms PCA, it opens up many promising multimodal and multiprofile configurations; if it underperforms, it suggests PCA is already near the representation ceiling and we should focus on profile/aggregation/fusion choices instead. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving the representation question early maximizes the information value of subsequent experiments.

Evidence: scVI_n200 (0.5203) outperforms PCA_n2000 (0.4849) as an RNA encoder, and image-only is very weak (0.2079), indicating RNA is the dominant signal. The key untested design axis is profile setting (single vs. multi). This experiment tests whether multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) with the best-performing encoder (scVI_n200) improves over the single-profile baseline (config_004). It isolates the profile-setting effect while holding the encoder fixed, using the simplest aggregation (avgpool) to first establish whether multiprofile adds value at all. If it helps, we can then explore transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion in subsequent experiments; if not, we save budget for encoder or fusion exploration. This is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step with 6 experiments remaining.

Evidence: config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) is the clear best at 0.650 acc, showing that multiprofile + scvi_n200 is a strong combination. The single largest gain so far came from singleprofile→multiprofile. Uncertainty: whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool for this encoder+profile setting. This experiment (config_006) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding scvi_n200 and multiprofile fixed, giving a clean single-variable comparison to config_005. It is the best use of the 5th slot because it directly exploits the most promising direction, isolates the aggregation effect, and the result will inform whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal transformer-fusion configs or to pivot to scgpt encoder testing.

Evidence: The current best (config_006, RNA-only/multi-profile/scVI_n200/transformer, acc=0.653) shows that multi-profile scVI_n200 is the dominant configuration, and transformer vs avgpool aggregation makes negligible difference. The only untested RNA encoder is scGPT. Question: Does scGPT outperform scVI_n200 as the RNA encoder in the multi-profile + transformer setting? This is a clean single-variable change from config_006. Why this is the best next experiment: With 4 experiments remaining, establishing whether scGPT offers a stronger RNA representation before committing budget to multimodal fusion is critical. If scGPT is superior, it becomes the foundation for the strongest multimodal configs; if not, we confirm scVI_n200 as the best encoder and can dedicate remaining budget to testing whether multimodal fusion adds value on top of the proven RNA-only best.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. Remaining RNA-only configs (PCA-based or scgpt-based) are unlikely to exceed this given PCA underperformed scvi_n200 (0.485 vs 0.520 single) and scgpt underperformed in multiprofile (0.514 vs 0.653). The key unexplored question is whether a stronger image encoder (ViT-L, vs the weak ResNet50 at 0.208) can add complementary signal via fusion. Config_039 pairs the proven best RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) with imagenet_vit_l and weighted fusion, which allows the model to adaptively downweight the image if it contributes little. This directly tests whether multimodal fusion can push past 0.653, and the result will determine whether the remaining 3 experiments should explore other fusion strategies/image encoders or confirm the RNA-only ceiling.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. The most informative single-variable comparison is config_038, which is identical except it uses concat fusion instead of weighted fusion. This directly tests whether the fusion strategy is a meaningful lever for improvement or whether weighted fusion is already near-optimal. In the RNA-only setting, aggregation choice (transformer vs avgpool) made negligible difference, so the fusion mechanism is the more likely source of remaining variance. If concat outperforms weighted, we find a new best; if not, we confirm the current best's fusion choice and can use the remaining 2 experiments to explore other dimensions (e.g., avgpool aggregation in config_037). This is the highest-information single-change experiment available for the current top configuration.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. Evidence shows scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, and weighted fusion are all strong choices. The one remaining untested variant closest to the best is the aggregation method: in the RNA-only setting, transformer (0.653) and avgpool (0.650) were nearly equivalent, and in the multimodal setting we've only tested transformer with both fusion types. Config_037 (avgpool + weighted) isolates whether aggregation method matters in the multimodal context. If it matches or exceeds 0.725, it reveals a better configuration; if not, it confirms config_039 as the robust optimum. With only 1 experiment left after this, testing the closest untested neighbor of the current best is the highest-information, lowest-risk choice to either improve or confirm the final answer.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. The evidence strongly supports scVI_n200 as the best RNA encoder (outperforming PCA by ~0.04 and scGPT by ~0.14 in RNA-only), transformer aggregation over avgpool, weighted fusion over concat, and multiprofile over singleprofile. The only untested dimension within this optimal pipeline is the image encoder: ViT-L vs. ResNet50. While ResNet50 was very poor in isolation (0.2079 image-only), config_033 isolates whether a weaker image encoder in a weighted-fusion multimodal pipeline can still contribute or whether ViT-L's strength is essential. This is the most principled single-variable extension of the current best, keeping all other components at their validated optima. As the final experiment, it either confirms ViT-L's necessity or reveals a comparable alternative, maximizing information gain without compounding multiple uncertain changes.
